description: Synthesizes evidence-grounded executive narratives. Use when stakeholders need a concise process summary, key risks, and prioritized next actions.
use_when: stakeholders need a concise process summary, key risks, and prioritized next actions
prompt_instructions: Create a concise narrative with four sections: Context, Current Workflow, Key Risks, and Recommended Next Actions. Cite only provided evidence, flag assumptions explicitly, and keep recommendations actionable.
workflow_steps: Read process context and relevant evidence
Draft narrative using the required section structure
Validate claims against available evidence
Finalize concise output with prioritized next actions
acceptance_checks: Includes Context section
Summarizes workflow with evidence
Lists key risks
Lists prioritized next actions
Flags assumptions explicitly
sample_instruction: Draft an executive narrative for the current process, highlight top 3 risks, and recommend next actions for the next 30 days.

description: Produces RACI matrices with clear ownership and accountability. Use when teams need role clarity for activities, approvals, and handoffs.
use_when: teams need role clarity for activities, approvals, and handoffs
prompt_instructions: Generate a complete RACI table where each activity has one Accountable owner, at least one Responsible owner, and no blank critical assignments. Preserve role names consistently and call out unresolved ownership gaps. Apply patterns in backend/config/skills/raci_v2/deloitte_raci_leading_practices.md. Optional: python scripts/validate_raci_markdown.py on markdown tables.
workflow_steps: Extract activities and participating roles from context
Assign one Accountable and at least one Responsible per activity
Add Consulted and Informed roles where relevant
Validate for missing or conflicting ownership
acceptance_checks: Every activity has one A
Every activity has at least one R
No duplicate A per row
Ownership gaps are explicitly flagged
Export-ready table structure
sample_instruction: Create a RACI for onboarding, procurement, and monthly reporting with one accountable owner per activity and no missing assignments.

description: Generates implementation-ready SOPs with role ownership and control checks. Use when teams need standardized execution steps for recurring operations.
use_when: teams need standardized execution steps for recurring operations
prompt_instructions: Generate an SOP with sections for Purpose, Scope, Roles and Responsibilities, Procedure Steps, Control Checks, Escalation Path, and References. Use imperative language for steps and include measurable control points.
workflow_steps: Define purpose, scope, and roles
Draft ordered procedure steps in imperative style
Attach measurable control checks to key steps
Add escalation path and references
acceptance_checks: Contains Purpose and Scope
Defines role ownership
Lists step-by-step procedure
Includes control checks
Includes escalation path
sample_instruction: Draft an SOP for invoice processing with clear roles, controls, escalation rules, and references to related policies.

description: Builds lane-aware process maps with decisions and handoffs. Use when teams need a visual model of sequence, ownership, and branching logic.
use_when: teams need a visual model of sequence, ownership, and branching logic
prompt_instructions: Generate a diagrams.net compatible process map with Start and End nodes, swimlanes by role, decision points with labeled branches, and consistent top-to-bottom flow. Ensure handoffs align to lane ownership. Use backend/config/skills/process_map_v2/deloitte_process_mapping_leading_practices.md and backend/config/skills/process_map_v2/sap_activate_process_alignment.md for SAP-aligned workshops.
workflow_steps: Identify actors, steps, and decision points
Lay out swimlanes by role ownership
Connect sequence and decision branches with labels
Validate start/end nodes, handoffs, and flow consistency
feedback_loop: Fix disconnected nodes and lane mismatches
acceptance_checks: Includes Start and End nodes
Uses swimlanes by role
Decision branches are labeled and connected
Flow direction is consistent
Handoffs match lane ownership
sample_instruction: Create a swimlane process map for customer complaint handling with decision branches for severity and escalation.

description: Creates, edits, and analyzes Word .docx files with structure, formatting, and tracked-change aware workflows. Use when a task requires producing or modifying professional Word documents.
use_when: a task requires creating, reading, editing, or restructuring Word .docx files
prompt_instructions: Generate or update .docx outputs using a deterministic workflow: read requirements, draft structure, apply formatting rules, validate content/layout, and finalize. Preserve template conventions when editing existing files.
workflow_steps: Capture deliverable intent and document constraints
Draft section structure and required formatting elements
Produce or edit .docx content while preserving template conventions
Validate structure, consistency, and output readiness
acceptance_checks: Document structure matches requested format
Formatting is consistent and professional
Template conventions are preserved for edits
No unresolved placeholder content
sample_instruction: Create a polished .docx project memo with title page, section headings, table, and footer page numbers.

description: Applies distinctive, production-grade frontend-inspired aesthetics (typography, hierarchy, spacing) to DOCX-ready markdown content.
use_when: the user wants a docx artifact that feels visually intentional and well-structured (frontend-inspired design language), not generic layouts
prompt_instructions:
Use a bold aesthetic direction (typography hierarchy + spacing + compositional choices) before writing. Then produce ONLY DOCX-ready markdown that will convert cleanly to Word:
- Use clear heading levels and short, intentional section titles.
- Prefer bullet lists and concise paragraphs; separate sections with blank lines to preserve whitespace.
- Avoid any HTML/CSS/React code, and do not use fenced code blocks.
- Do not follow generic AI aesthetics; make layout choices feel cohesive and intentional.

CRITICAL OUTPUT CONTRACT: Return ONLY markdown text compatible with our DOCX markdown-to-DOCX writer.
workflow_steps: Pick a bold aesthetic direction and define the typographic hierarchy
Outline the DOCX sections with concise, readable headings
Draft markdown content with spacing and bullet structure
Self-check for generic filler and formatting that converts cleanly to DOCX
acceptance_checks: Clear typographic/section hierarchy using markdown headings
Concise bullet/paragraph structure with readable whitespace
No HTML/CSS/React code or fenced code blocks
No generic AI aesthetic patterns; choices feel intentional
sample_instruction: Create a DOCX executive memo with a distinctive, refined visual hierarchy (headings + bullets + spacing) using a cohesive aesthetic direction, while keeping output as plain markdown.

description: Applies distinctive, production-grade frontend-inspired aesthetics to PPTX slide blueprint output.
use_when: the user wants slides with intentional visual hierarchy and cohesive aesthetic direction (frontend-inspired), while still producing valid JSON blueprints
prompt_instructions:
Choose a bold aesthetic direction first (minimal vs maximalist, refined vs playful) and then design the slide blueprint around it.

CRITICAL OUTPUT CONTRACT: Return ONLY a valid JSON object with key `slides`.
- Each slide: {"title": string, "bullets": string[]}
- Keep bullets concise (max 6 per slide) and design for scannability.
- Use titles and bullets that reflect the chosen aesthetic direction through clear hierarchy (short titles, meaningful ordering).
- Avoid generic filler; make the deck feel intentional and cohesive.

No additional text besides the JSON.
workflow_steps: Pick an aesthetic direction and define deck-wide hierarchy
Draft slide titles in an ordered narrative flow
Generate concise bullet points that emphasize key ideas
Validate the JSON-only output contract
acceptance_checks: Valid JSON with `slides` key and slide objects
Concise scannable bullet points
Cohesive slide ordering and hierarchy consistent with the aesthetic direction
No non-JSON text in the output
sample_instruction: Create a PPTX blueprint deck with a bold aesthetic direction using cohesive slide hierarchy; output must be ONLY JSON as our pptx agent expects.

description: Applies frontend-inspired clarity and structure to XLSX-convertible markdown table content.
use_when: the user wants an XLSX artifact that is clean, readable, and structured like a well-designed frontend table (consistent labels, minimal clutter)
prompt_instructions:
Choose a clear table organization principle (consistency + scannability) before writing.

CRITICAL OUTPUT CONTRACT: Return ONLY the markdown table rows (no commentary, no code fences).
- Use consistent wording in column cells (no random synonyms for the same concept).
- Keep each cell concise to reduce visual clutter after XLSX conversion.
- Ensure the header and divider row are included exactly once.

Do not output HTML/CSS/JS or any extra text beyond the markdown table.
workflow_steps: Select a consistent labeling scheme for table content
Draft a clean markdown table with our fixed column structure
Tighten wording for scannability and readability
Validate the markdown-table-only output contract
acceptance_checks: Output is ONLY a markdown table (header + divider + rows)
Consistent cell labeling and minimal clutter
No HTML/CSS/JS and no extra commentary
Cells are concise and readable after XLSX conversion
sample_instruction: Create an XLSX-ready markdown table with a clean, frontend-like information hierarchy; output must be ONLY the markdown table.

description: Creates, edits, and validates spreadsheet models with formulas, formatting, and tabular transformations. Use when the primary deliverable is an Excel-compatible spreadsheet.
use_when: the main input or output is xlsx, xlsm, csv, or tsv and the deliverable must be a spreadsheet
prompt_instructions: Build spreadsheet outputs with formulas instead of hardcoded calculations, preserve template conventions when updating existing files, and run formula/error validation before finalizing.
workflow_steps: Inspect source data and workbook structure
Apply transformations and formulas in spreadsheet form
Format with consistent professional standards
Validate for formula and reference errors before delivery
acceptance_checks: No formula errors (#REF!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #N/A, #NAME?)
Formulas are used for calculations instead of hardcoded derived values
Output preserves or matches required template conventions
Workbook is delivery-ready and readable
sample_instruction: Create an xlsx model with assumptions sheet, monthly revenue forecast formulas, and summary dashboard table.

description: Creates, edits, and validates presentation decks with layout, visual hierarchy, and slide-quality checks. Use when deliverables involve .pptx files, decks, or slides.
use_when: a task requires creating, updating, parsing, or repackaging powerpoint presentations
prompt_instructions: Produce .pptx slides with clear visual hierarchy, consistent spacing, and strong contrast. Use a quality loop to detect overflow, overlap, alignment, and placeholder-content issues before final output.
workflow_steps: Define narrative and slide-level structure
Build or edit slides with intentional visual design
Run content and visual QA checks
Fix layout/content defects and finalize deck
acceptance_checks: Slides have consistent hierarchy and spacing
No text overflow or overlapping elements
No leftover placeholder content
Deck supports intended narrative flow
sample_instruction: Build a 10-slide executive deck summarizing current-state process issues, opportunities, and a 90-day action plan.

description: Processes PDF files for extraction, transformation, composition, and form-oriented workflows. Use when users need to read, merge, split, create, or convert PDF content.
use_when: a task mentions pdf input/output, including extraction, form handling, or document assembly
prompt_instructions: Handle PDF operations with a task-specific workflow: identify operation type, execute extraction or transformation, validate output completeness, and finalize in the requested format.
workflow_steps: Identify PDF operation goal (extract, merge, split, create, transform)
Execute operation using appropriate processing path
Validate extracted/generated output quality
Finalize and package requested artifacts
acceptance_checks: Output matches requested PDF operation
Extracted content is complete and legible
Generated artifacts open without errors
No unresolved processing failures
sample_instruction: Extract text and tables from a quarterly-report PDF and produce a clean, structured output package.

description: Creates CFO-grade Finance Transformation proposals and pitch decks for FP&A, close optimization, finance operating model, management reporting, treasury, finance digitization, and enterprise-wide transformation.
use_when: the user asks to draft a finance transformation proposal, RFP response, capability statement, or CFO pitch deck
prompt_instructions: Use the Finance Transformation proposal method from proposal-finance-transformation.skill. Always structure the deliverable with the 10-section framework, identify the FT sub-type up front, and enforce CFO-language outcomes (close days, forecast accuracy, working-capital impact, finance cost levers). For client gaps, use bracketed placeholders with content prompts. For PPTX, produce deck-ready narrative with sectioned slide flow; for DOCX, produce narrative-ready proposal sections. Align with Deloitte-style proposal patterns in backend/config/skills/proposal_finance_transformation_v1/deloitte_proposal_leading_practices.md (client-first arc, CFO metrics, risks). Optional: python scripts/check_proposal_signals.py on markdown.
workflow_steps: Identify Finance Transformation sub-type and target format (PPTX or DOCX)
Gather/derive client context, benchmarks, and finance pain points
Draft all 10 required proposal sections with FT-specific content
Run QA checks for CFO-language value metrics, benchmark anchoring, and no blank fields
feedback_loop: Validate FT specificity and benchmark usage
Strengthen CFO-value articulation and risk register quality
acceptance_checks: All 10 proposal sections are present and labeled
Finance Transformation sub-type is explicitly identified and consistent throughout
Executive summary opens with the client finance problem, not firm credentials
Client understanding section is benchmark-anchored and client-specific
Commercial/value summary uses CFO-readable metrics
sample_instruction: Draft a Finance Transformation proposal for close acceleration and FP&A redesign, including a PPTX pitch deck and a DOCX narrative variant with CFO-centric value metrics.

description: Applies brand colors and typography standards to presentation and document artifacts. Use when output needs to follow defined visual identity guidelines.
use_when: users request brand-compliant styling, visual consistency, or company-standard formatting
prompt_instructions: Apply Deloitte visual identity consistently across all deliverables. Use Deloitte Green as the primary accent (#86BC25), with supporting neutral palette (#000000, #333333, #666666, #F3F4F6, #FFFFFF). Keep layouts clean and executive-ready: strong heading hierarchy, generous whitespace, and restrained color usage. Preferred typography behavior: clear sans-serif hierarchy (Heading: semibold/bold; Body: regular), sentence case, and high contrast for accessibility. For PPTX, use concise slide titles, left-aligned content grids, and minimal decorative elements; for DOCX/PDF use structured headings, consistent paragraph spacing, and professional table styling with subtle header fills. Never use conflicting bright palettes or low-contrast text/background combinations.
workflow_steps: Capture target artifact type and styling scope
Apply brand colors and typography hierarchy
Review contrast, readability, and consistency
Finalize brand-compliant output
acceptance_checks: Brand colors and typography are applied consistently
Text contrast and readability are preserved
Heading/body style hierarchy is clear
Output reflects requested brand identity
sample_instruction: Restyle an existing executive summary and slide content to match approved brand colors and typography rules.

description: Creates structured Approach Notes that define how a problem should be solved and why. Use when users ask for an approach note, methodology note, POV, thinking note, or strategic framework document.
use_when: the user asks to write or draft an approach note, methodology note, POV, method paper, approach paper, diagnostic note, strategic framework document, or asks how we should approach this problem
prompt_instructions: Use the approach-note method from approach-note.skill. Produce an argument-led Approach Note using the 7 required sections: Problem Framing, Why the Standard Approach Fails, Our Hypothesis, The Proposed Approach, What We Will Learn and When, Risks and Intellectual Limitations, and Conclusion with Decision Request. Enforce hypothesis-first writing, explicit evidence level, and epistemic honesty. Distinguish this from sales proposals and status reporting. Default to DOCX-oriented structure, with structured markdown fallback when DOCX is not requested. Use backend/config/skills/approach_note_v1/deloitte_approach_note_leading_practices.md for evidence grading and decision asks. Optional: python scripts/check_approach_sections.py on markdown.
workflow_steps: Identify use context (pre-proposal, client-facing, or practice development)
Bound the problem statement and gather constraints, knowns, and unknowns
Draft all 7 sections with falsifiable hypothesis and method-specific approach
Run QA checks for rigor, non-generic language, and decision-oriented conclusion
feedback_loop: Validate hypothesis quality and evidence strength
Strengthen Section 02, Section 05, and limitations where weak
Finalize output with a clear decision request
acceptance_checks: All 7 Approach Note sections are present
Hypothesis is falsifiable and causal (not a task list)
Standard approach failure mode is explicit and non-trivial
At least 2 falsification signals are listed
Conclusion requests a specific decision or action
sample_instruction: Draft a client-facing approach note for finance transformation that argues why the standard assessment model fails, states a falsifiable hypothesis, and proposes a method-specific plan with risks and decision request.

description: Creates formal, traceable Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) with functional and non-functional requirements. Use when users ask for BRD, FRD, requirements specification, or requirement registers.
use_when: the user asks to write, create, or draft a BRD, requirements specification, functional specification, FRD, requirements register, or asks to document what the system/process must do
prompt_instructions: Use the BRD method from brd.skill. Produce a 10-section BRD that clearly separates requirements from solution design: Executive Overview, Scope, Stakeholders and User Roles, Current State Baseline, Assumptions/Dependencies/Constraints, Functional Requirements, Non-Functional Requirements, Data Requirements, Reporting and Output Requirements, and Governance/Traceability/Sign-off. Enforce EARS syntax for functional requirements, MoSCoW priority, requirement IDs, and measurable non-functional criteria. Default to DOCX as the authoritative artifact, with PPTX summary output when requested. Deepen with backend/config/skills/brd_v1/deloitte_brd_leading_practices.md (traceability, RTM) and backend/config/skills/brd_v1/sap_s4hana_requirements_primer.md for SAP/S/4HANA. Optional: python scripts/check_brd_sections.py on markdown.
workflow_steps: Identify BRD type (system, process, integration, or report) and domain context
Collect and bound scope, stakeholders, objectives, assumptions, and constraints
Draft all 10 sections with traceable functional and non-functional requirements
Run QA checks for EARS syntax, ID traceability, MoSCoW prioritization, and measurable NFRs
feedback_loop: Fix ambiguity, missing traceability, or solution leakage
Finalize with sign-off and change-control clarity
acceptance_checks: All 10 BRD sections are present and labeled
Functional requirements use EARS syntax and unique IDs
Each requirement has a MoSCoW priority
Non-functional requirements are measurable and compliance-specific where applicable
Governance includes traceability, sign-off authority, and change control
sample_instruction: Draft a BRD for an FP&A planning platform with EARS-based functional requirements, measurable NFRs, MoSCoW priorities, traceability IDs, and an optional stakeholder summary deck.
